final:
I made both files in `public/models/`, and each one keeps the tool's "no visible quality loss" threshold. That threshold is a worst-region SSIM of at least 0.9, measured against the original over 4 views at 1024px. Neither file is better on every measure, so the choice is yours.

| | original | `lantern-small.glb` | `lantern-gpu.glb` |
|---|---|---|---|
| Download | 9.56 MB | **0.221 MB** (43× smaller) | 2.43 MB (3.9× smaller) |
| GPU memory | 85.6 MiB | 21.5 MiB (4× less) | **5.5 MiB** (15.6× less) |
| Load time on 4g (download plus decode) | 9.1 s | **0.39 s** | 2.85 s |
| Fidelity (worst-region SSIM, threshold 0.9) | – | 0.90 (right at the limit) | 0.95 |
| Textures | 4× PNG 2048² | 4× AVIF 1024² | 4× KTX2 UASTC 1024² |
| Geometry | – | meshopt | quantized |
| Decoder in the viewer | – | meshopt (6 KB gzip) | KTX2 (260 KB gzip) |

Triangles are unchanged at 5,394 in both.

**Trade-off in numbers:**
- **Download:** the small version is about 11× smaller than the GPU version (0.22 MB vs 2.43 MB).
- **GPU memory:** the GPU version uses about 4× less (5.5 vs 21.5 MiB). The AVIF textures in the small version are decoded to full 1024² RGBA on the GPU. KTX2 stays compressed on the GPU.
- **Fidelity:** the small version sits exactly at the 0.90 limit, so it has no margin. The GPU version has more headroom at 0.95.
- **Load time:** the GPU version costs about 2.4 s more on 4g, mostly from its 2.4 MB of textures.

**Which to pick:**
- If the lantern is a one-off on a typical desktop viewer, the small version is almost certainly better. It loads in 0.4 s and 21 MiB is negligible.
- Choose the GPU version if it will sit in a scene with many other assets or run on memory-constrained mobile GPUs.

**Compatibility:**
- Babylon.js loads both decoders automatically, as the tool's warnings say.
- The small file needs `EXT_texture_avif`, so check that your Babylon version and target browsers support AVIF. The GPU file's KTX2 path has no such dependency.
- I didn't open either file in your viewer. All numbers come from `node-assets` measurements in headless Chromium.

The recipes and the full candidate table are in `recipes/` if you want to re-run with different settings. My first tune attempt was killed by a timeout and produced nothing. The second run completed and is what these files come from.
bash_cmds: node-assets tune assets/lantern.glb --for size,gpu -o recipes/ 2>&1 | tail -50; ls recipes
until [ -n "$(ls recipes 2>/dev/null)" ]; do sleep 5; done; ls recipes
ps aux | grep -c "[n]ode-assets\|[b]in.mjs"; ps aux | grep "[b]in.mjs" | head -3
for i in $(seq 1 55); do kill -0 17588 2>/dev/null || break; sleep 5; done; ls recipes; ps -p 17588 -o etime=
node-assets tune assets/lantern.glb --for size,gpu -o recipes/ --time-limit 5m > tune.log 2>&1; echo exit $?; tail -40 tune.log; ls recipes

node-assets run recipes/lantern.size.recipe.toon assets/lantern.glb -o public/models/lantern-small.glb 2>&1 | tail -15; node-assets run recipes/lantern.gpu.recipe.toon assets/lantern.glb -o public/models/lantern-gpu.glb 2>&1 | tail -15; node-assets inspect public/models/lantern-small.glb public/models/lantern-gpu.glb --against assets/lantern.glb 2>&1 | tail -40
